patches.expectedValueJson: "article 经由法语传入英语，来源可追溯到拉丁语 articulus。历史上，这个拉丁词可表示“部分”或“关节”；文章的分段、条款和单件物品等用法与“一个部分或单独的一件”这一概念相连。语法术语有古老的比喻背景，但古代语法分类与现代英语冠词并不完全相同。"

sourceEvidence.text: Article came through French from Latin articulus, which could refer to a part or member and was related to artus, a joint. Early English uses involved separate clauses or sections of writing; later uses included a self-contained piece in a publication and an individual item. The grammatical term has an ancient joint metaphor, but Latin and Greek grammatical categories do not exactly match modern English articles.
